Representation theory of the symmetric group

 Home Mathematics Area of mathematics Algebra Representation theory
OurBigBook.com Words: 8k Articles: 151
The representation theory of Sn​ is organized by a partition of an integer. Over the complex numbers, partitions label the irreducible Specht modules; over positive-characteristic fields, the simple modules are labelled by regular partitions.

Induction ring of symmetric-group characters (⨁n≥0​R(Sn​))

Words: 69
Representation theory of the symmetric group OurBigBook.com
The graded abelian group ⨁n≥0​R(Sn​) of ordinary virtual characters has product χ⋆ψ=IndSm​×Sn​Sm+n​​(χ⊠ψ) for degrees m,n. Its unit is the trivial degree-zero character. Associativity follows by transitivity of induced representations through the three-factor Young subgroup; commutativity follows by conjugating the block positions. The Frobenius characteristic map identifies this ring with the ring of symmetric functions, sending irreducible Specht characters to Schur functions. This product is different from pointwise multiplication of characters of the same symmetric group.

Symmetric-group characters are integer-valued (χλ(g)∈Z)

Words: 40
Representation theory of the symmetric group OurBigBook.com
The character of a Young permutation module counts fixed tabloids and is integer-valued. Dominance order on partitions makes its decomposition into Specht modules triangular with diagonal multiplicity one. Descending induction in any order refining dominance therefore expresses each irreducible Specht character as an integer combination of permutation characters, proving integrality.

Young subgroup (Sλ​)

Words: 44
Representation theory of the symmetric group OurBigBook.com
For a composition λ of n, a Young subgroup permutes independently the blocks of a set partition of {1,…,n} with sizes λi​, and is isomorphic to Sλ1​​×⋯×Sλr​​. Reordering the block sizes gives a conjugate subgroup. Inducing its trivial representation gives a Young permutation module.

Skew representation of a symmetric group (Vλ/μ)

Words: 56
Representation theory of the symmetric group OurBigBook.com
For ∣λ∣=n, ∣μ∣=m, and k=n−m, define
Vλ/μ=HomSm​​(Vμ,ResSm​Sn​​Vλ).
(1)
The copy of Sk​ acting on the last k letters commutes with Sm​ and acts on this multiplicity space. Iterated restriction branching rule for a symmetric group supplies a basis indexed by standard skew Young tableaux. Every such basis vector is a cyclic vector for a group representation: admissible swaps connect all tableaux, and their off-diagonal coefficients in the Young orthogonal form are nonzero.

Deletion projection for a symmetric group (Πn​)

Words: 77
Representation theory of the symmetric group OurBigBook.com
Delete n from the cycle notation of a permutation in Sn​ to obtain a permutation in Sn−1​. Extend this set map linearly to Πn​:CSn​→CSn−1​. It is an Sn−1​-bimodule map and the identity on CSn−1​, but is not in general an algebra homomorphism. In particular,
Πn​(Xn​)=(n−1)1,Πn​(Xn2​)=(n−1)1+2∑i<j<n​(i j).
(2)
For n≥5 it is the unique bimodule-equivariant set map Sn​→Sn−1​; at n=4 another such map exists because CS3​​(S2​)=S2​.

Gelfand–Tsetlin algebra (GZn​)

Words: 545 Articles: 8
Representation theory of the symmetric group OurBigBook.com
For the chain S0​⊂⋯⊂Sn​, the Gelfand–Tsetlin algebra in CSn​ is generated by the centers of CSr​ for 0≤r≤n. Multiplicity-free restriction makes its joint eigenspaces one-dimensional in each irreducible representation. Products of the central primitive idempotents along restriction paths give its minimal projections. Thus it is a maximal commutative subalgebra and a semisimple algebra, isomorphic to a finite product of copies of C.

Jucys–Murphy description of the center of a symmetric-group algebra (Z(FSn​)={f(J1​,…,Jn​):f symmetric})

Words: 61
Jucys–Murphy element OurBigBook.com
The Young–Jucys–Murphy elements commute, and symmetric polynomials in them are central. The full center theorem holds integrally as well as over fields, so it survives modular reduction. On an ordinary Specht module, the scalar of such a polynomial is its value on the cell-content multiset. The integral generation step is stronger than knowing this description only over a characteristic-zero field and is essential in the modular block argument.

Cycle-sum identity for Young–Jucys–Murphy elements (X2​⋯Xn​=∑π an n-cycle​π)

Words: 80
Jucys–Murphy element OurBigBook.com
In the group algebra of Sn​, the product of the Young–Jucys–Murphy elements X2​,…,Xn​ is the sum of all n-cycles, each with coefficient one. To prove it, multiply the sum of all m-cycles by Xm+1​. Right multiplication by (j m+1) inserts m+1 immediately after j in the cycle. Every (m+1)-cycle has a unique predecessor of m+1, so deletion inverts this insertion bijectively. Induction starts at X2​=(1 2). The identity turns a product of cell contents into a central character value of a conjugacy-class sum.

Local spectral rules for Young–Jucys–Murphy elements

Words: 56
Jucys–Murphy element OurBigBook.com
For the joint spectrum of the Young–Jucys–Murphy elements, adjacent coordinates ai​,ai+1​ are distinct. If ai+1​−ai​=±1, the adjacent transposition si​ acts on that line by ±1. Otherwise interchanging the coordinates gives a spectral vector in the same irreducible representation. These rules follow from si​Xi​si​+si​=Xi+1​ and its two-dimensional eigenspace calculation. Together with the braid relation in a Coxeter group, they exclude the consecutive patterns (a,a±1,a).

Olshanskii centralizer lemma

Words: 62
Jucys–Murphy element OurBigBook.com
For the standard inclusion Sn−1​⊂Sn​, over the complex numbers,
CCSn​​(CSn−1​)=alg(Z(CSn−1​),Xn​).
(4)
Here Xn​ is a Young–Jucys–Murphy element. One way to see generation is to use multiplicity-free restriction: a central idempotent of Sn−1​ selects a preceding shape, and the distinct contents of its addable nodes of a Young diagram distinguish all possible succeeding shapes. Polynomial interpolation in Xn​ supplies every diagonal projection in the centralizer of a subalgebra.

Gelfand–Tsetlin basis

Words: 178 Articles: 2
Gelfand–Tsetlin algebra OurBigBook.com
Successively decompose an irreducible representation along a subgroup chain with multiplicity-free restriction. A complete path selects a one-dimensional subspace; choosing one nonzero vector on each path gives a Gelfand–Tsetlin basis. For a symmetric group over the complex numbers, paths are standard Young tableaux, and the Young–Jucys–Murphy elements act diagonally with their cell contents.

Young seminormal form

Words: 135 Articles: 1
Gelfand–Tsetlin basis OurBigBook.com
Let T be a standard Young tableau, si​=(i i+1), and d=cT​(i+1)−cT​(i). A suitable Gelfand–Tsetlin basis has, for an admissible pair R=si​T with tableau length increasing,
si​vT​=d−1vT​+vR​,si​vR​=(1−d−2)vT​−d−1vR​.
(5)
For a nonadmissible swap the scalar is +1 in a row and −1 in a column. The diagonal coefficient follows from the Young–Jucys–Murphy element relation si​Xi​si​+si​=Xi+1​, and si2​=1 forces the product of off-diagonal coefficients. One global normalization is vT​=PT​πT​vT0​​ from the row-reading tableau: a reduced admissible path makes this vector nonzero and gives coefficient one on every length-increasing edge.
Young orthogonal form
Words: 52
Young seminormal form OurBigBook.com
Normalizing the tableau lines in a compatible real phase convention gives the orthonormal basis form
si​​span(wT​,wsi​T​)​=(d−11−d−2​​1−d−2​−d−1​),d=cT​(i+1)−cT​(i).
(6)
Admissible swaps have ∣d∣≥2. Nonadmissible swaps act by +1 within a row and −1 within a column. The symmetric matrix is an orthogonal involution and is useful for making the unitary representation and its phases explicit.

Sign representation (sgn)

Words: 31
Representation theory of the symmetric group OurBigBook.com
The sign representation of Sn​ is the one-dimensional representation in which a permutation acts by its sign. Tensoring a representation by it multiplies its character value at g by sgn(g).

Prime-degree irreducible Kronecker product criterion for a symmetric group

Words: 58
Tensor identity for an induced character OurBigBook.com
Let n be prime. If the Kronecker product χαχβ of two irreducible characters of Sn​ is irreducible, then one of α,β is (n) or (1n). Comparing the two self-products shows that only one may contain the standard character; the restriction branching rule then makes one partition rectangular, and primality makes that rectangle a single row or column.

Partition of an integer

Words: 6k Articles: 130
Representation theory of the symmetric group OurBigBook.com
A partition λ⊢n is a weakly decreasing sequence λ1​≥λ2​≥⋯≥0 with sum n.

Reverse lexicographic order on partitions (λ<R​μ⟺λi​>μi​ at the first difference)

Words: 51
Partition of an integer OurBigBook.com
Pad partitions with trailing zeros. In the descending-dictionary convention used for symmetric-function reverse lexicographic ordering, the partition with the larger first differing part precedes the other. This is the reverse of increasing dictionary order on integer partitions, and is a total order. It is distinct from comparing the last differing part in a monomial reverse-lexicographic order.

Glaisher partition bijection

Words: 89
Partition of an integer OurBigBook.com
Fix a prime p. Replace each part pam, with p∤m, by pa copies of m. This is a size-preserving bijection from regular partitions to partitions of an integer whose parts are not divisible by p. To invert it, write each multiplicity of a part m not divisible by p in base p and use its digit in position a as the multiplicity of pam. Every resulting multiplicity is below p. The bijection explains why the number of simple symmetric-group modules equals the number of p-regular elements' conjugacy classes.

Dictionary order on integer partitions (λ>μ⟺λk​>μk​ at the first difference)

Words: 42
Partition of an integer OurBigBook.com
Pad partitions with trailing zeros and compare their first unequal parts. A partition is larger in dictionary order on integer partitions when that first unequal part is larger. This is a total order, whereas dominance order on partitions compares every prefix sum and is generally partial. The row-column collision lemma links these two orders.

Young's lattice (Y)

Words: 150 Articles: 2
Partition of an integer OurBigBook.com
The Young lattice is a partially ordered set whose elements are integer partitions, including the empty partition. Each partition of an integer is identified with its diagram, and the order is inclusion of Young diagrams. A cover adds exactly one box. A saturated path from the empty diagram to λ is equivalent to a standard Young tableau of shape λ.

Young branching graph

Words: 100 Articles: 1
Young's lattice OurBigBook.com
The Young branching graph is the graded cover graph of the Young lattice. Its level n consists of partitions of n, and its edges add one box. It is also the branching graph for complex Specht modules under the restriction branching rule for a symmetric group.
Oscillating path in the Young lattice
Words: 62
Young branching graph OurBigBook.com
An oscillating tableau is a sequence of Young diagrams, each obtained from its predecessor by adding or removing one box. These are paths in the Young branching graph with both directions allowed. A path of length ℓ from the empty diagram to λ⊢n, with ℓ−n=2m≥0, has count ℓ!fλ​/(2mn!m!). This differs from a saturated upward path, whose length must equal n.

∏i=1e​1−xi1​.

Skew Young diagram (λ/μ)

Words: 254 Articles: 4
Young diagram OurBigBook.com
For diagram inclusion μ⊆λ, the skew Young diagram λ/μ consists of the cells of λ outside μ. Diagram inclusion is not the dominance order on partitions. Edge adjacency defines its connected components, and a connected skew diagram without a 2×2 square is a rim hook.
Standard skew Young tableau
Words: 97 Articles: 1
Skew Young diagram OurBigBook.com
A standard skew Young tableau fills the k cells of a skew Young diagram bijectively with 1,…,k, increasing along each row and column. Equivalently it is a linear extension of a partially ordered set formed from the row and column inequalities. Interchanging consecutive labels preserves standardness exactly when their cells are incomparable in that partial order.

Words: 50
Standard skew Young tableau OurBigBook.com
Here n=∣λ∣−∣μ∣, with zero entries for negative factorial arguments. Extract the squarefree monomial x1​⋯xn​ from the skew Jacobi–Trudi identity. A product hr1​​⋯hrℓ​​ contributes n!/∏ri​! because its distinct labels are assigned to the factors in that many ways. Summing determinant signs proves the formula, since a squarefree semistandard Young tableau is a standard skew Young tableau.
Horizontal strip
Words: 60
Skew Young diagram OurBigBook.com
A horizontal strip is a skew Young diagram containing at most one cell in each column. Equivalently, λ/μ is a horizontal strip when λi​≥μi​≥λi+1​ for all i. The multiplicity of the trivial representation in the associated skew representation of a symmetric group is one for horizontal strips and zero otherwise. A column with two cells supplies a cyclic tableau vector on which an adjacent transposition acts by −1, excluding invariants.
Totally disconnected skew Young diagram
Words: 54
Skew Young diagram OurBigBook.com
Under edge adjacency, a skew Young diagram is totally disconnected when every component has one cell. This means that no two cells share an edge. It is stronger than being a horizontal strip, which excludes repeated columns but permits adjacent cells in one row. The trivial-constituent criterion for a skew representation of a symmetric group concerns horizontal strips, not total disconnection in this sense.

Hook partition ((n−k,1k))

Words: 52
Young diagram OurBigBook.com
A hook partition has shape (n−k,1k), 0≤k≤n−1. Equivalently its Young diagram has no cell (2,2), so its only cell of content zero is (1,1). Its standard Young tableaux are counted by (kn−1​): choose the k entries below the initial 1, then the column and remaining row orders are forced.

Addable node of a Young diagram (λ+)

Words: 37
Young diagram OurBigBook.com
An addable node is a cell outside a Young diagram whose insertion leaves a Young diagram. Its left and upper predecessors, when present in the positive-coordinate grid, must already belong to the diagram. Different addable nodes have distinct Young-diagram cell contents.

Removable node of a Young diagram

Words: 28
Young diagram OurBigBook.com
A removable node is a cell whose deletion leaves a Young diagram. The set λ− consists of the distinct partitions obtained by deleting one removable node from λ.

Conjugate partition

Words: 28
Young diagram OurBigBook.com
The conjugate partition λ′ is obtained by reflecting the Young diagram across its main diagonal; thus λj′​ is the number of parts of λ at least j.

hi,j​(λ)=λi​−j+λj′​−i+1.

Hook length (hi,j​(λ))
Words: 113 Articles: 2
Hook of a Young diagram OurBigBook.com
The hook length of cell (i,j) in the Young diagram of a partition of an integer λ is the number of cells in its Young-diagram hook:
hi,j​(λ)=λi​−j+λj′​−i+1.

Here λ′ is the conjugate partition. There is one hook length for every cell, so the multiset of hook lengths has cardinality ∣λ∣.
Hook graph of a partition

Hook length OurBigBook.com
The hook graph is the Young diagram with the hook length written in each box. It displays the hook product and thus the hook-length formula for the corresponding Specht module. This use of the name is recorded in Frame, Robinson and Thrall's original hook-graph paper; it refers to a labeled array, not a directed hook-walk graph.

Divisor closure of hook lengths
Words: 51
Hook of a Young diagram OurBigBook.com
If a partition has a hook of length ef, it has a hook of length e. In a beta set, the first hook is a bead-gap pair at distance ef; along the arithmetic progression with step e, some consecutive pair changes from a bead to a gap.
Rim hook
Words: 100 Articles: 1
Hook of a Young diagram OurBigBook.com
A rim hook, or border strip, is a connected skew Young diagram containing no 2×2 square. Its leg length is one less than its number of occupied rows.
Border-strip tableau (μ=λ(0)⊆⋯⊆λ(ℓ)=λ)
Words: 72
Rim hook OurBigBook.com

A Specht filtration is a finite chain of submodules whose successive quotients are Specht modules. In positive characteristic it need not split and is not a composition series, because its Specht factors may themselves be reducible. Dimensions and ordinary lifted characters can still be added along the filtration.

A proof uses the restriction branching rule for a symmetric group: a nonstandard shape with at least two corners has two non-linear predecessors, and a rectangular shape has one predecessor which in turn has two non-linear predecessors. This bounds its degree strictly above n−1 once n≥9; the smaller cases follow directly from the hook-length formula.

Single-box up-move

Words: 85
Dominance order on partitions OurBigBook.com
A single-box up-move changes a partition of an integer by adding one to row i and subtracting one from row j>i, provided the result remains a partition. It increases exactly the partial sums ending between rows i and j−1. A partition μ dominates λ precisely when it is obtainable from λ by a sequence of these moves: fill the first deficient row from the row at the first return of the cumulative deficit to zero. This preserves the partition inequalities and decreases the distance to μ.
